Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register and then press the star key followed by the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star 2. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Emma Walsh, Chief Product Officer; Tyler Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer; and Nina Patel, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives across AI-powered observability, workflow automation, and multi-cloud analytics.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: expansion revenue from existing customers, free cash flow generation, advancing our product roadmap, CAC trends, achieving a strong Rule of 40 score, operating expense breakdown, customer mix evolution, and sales efficiency improvements. These efforts not only propelled our top-line growth but also underscored the scalability and stickiness of our platform.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $458 million, representing a 31% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin expanded to 82%, and operating income reached $95 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $1.2 billion, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Before I go into guidance, let me provide more color on those eight key areas Sarah highlighted, starting with one of our most critical growth drivers: expansion revenue from existing customers. In the SaaS world, sustainable hypergrowth comes from deepening penetration within our installed base through our land-and-expand model. Expansion revenue, which includes upsells, cross-sells, seat expansions, and usage-based uplift, represented 28% of total revenue this quarter at $128 million—a solid 37% year-over-year increase and up 12% quarter-over-quarter. This highlights the stickiness of our CloudForge Platform and helped drive our dollar-based net retention rate, or NRR, to 118% for the quarter, up from 115% in Q2 and ahead of the SaaS industry median of about 110% per recent Bessemer Venture Partners benchmarks.

Breaking it down, roughly 55% or $70 million came from net expansions in annual recurring revenue, or ARR, mainly from customers upgrading to higher tiers of our core Analytics Engine module. Average contract value for these expansions rose 22% year-over-year to $185,000, driven by demand for our AI-driven Predictive Insights add-on, with adoption exceeding 40% among enterprise accounts over $1 million in ARR—similar to Snowflake's uptake with Snowpark ML.

Cross-sells added another 30% or $38 million, as customers added products like our Security Posture Manager and Multi-Cloud Orchestrator. For instance, a top-5 financial services firm, much like ServiceNow's scaling of its Now Platform, started with our basic observability suite two years ago and expanded to full-stack governance across AWS, Azure, and GCP, contributing $2.4 million in incremental ARR this quarter. Seat expansions and usage-based growth accounted for the remaining 15% or $19 million, especially in our consumption pricing for data ingestion, where AI training workloads drove 25% month-over-month growth amid industry generative AI demands.

By region, North America was 72% of expansion at $92 million, up 41% year-over-year, as Fortune 500 firms in fintech and healthcare focus on multi-cloud resilience post-CrowdStrike outage. EMEA grew 52% to $24 million, supported by GDPR-compliant AI features and wins in DACH via partners like Deutsche Telekom. APAC, 14% of the mix at $12 million, accelerated 29% year-over-year in Japan and Singapore, though moderated by China's data rules.

These results come from our revamped customer success team with 15% more CSMs per cohort, cutting expansion velocity to 6 months for mid-market; product-led growth with 62% self-serve expansions via our Usage Intelligence dashboard; and deeper integrations to 150+ apps, including Databricks and Okta, unlocking cross-sells in 35% of top customers. Looking ahead, we see expansion at $144-156 million in Q4, implying NRR over 120% with Cortex AI 2.0 rollout, positioning us ahead of Datadog or New Relic as McKinsey forecasts expansions driving 60% of SaaS revenue by 2027.

Moving to free cash flow, which showcases our model's scalability and discipline. We generated $128 million in Q3 FY2024, or 28% of revenue—a 42% year-over-year jump from $90 million and up sequentially from $112 million in Q2. Trailing twelve months, FCF is $512 million, or 27% margin, beating the peer median of 20% per Bessemer's State of the Cloud.

Key drivers: First, revenue momentum with 31% growth to $458 million subscription revenue, NRR at 112% from expansions in CloudForge Collaborate. Large enterprises averaged $450K ACV new logos, expanding 25% in year one via AI workflow modules akin to Salesforce Einstein. DSO improved to 52 days with automated invoicing.

Second, operating leverage: Adjusted operating cash flow $142 million or 31% of revenue, up 38% year-over-year. Gross margins up 250 bps to 82% from AWS optimizations reducing compute costs 18%. CAC payback to 14 months via PLG, freemium conversions at 8.2%. R&D at 22% of revenue from productivity tools like GitHub Copilot, shipping 15 features.

Third, capex $14 million or 3% of revenue, down 30% year-over-year after data center buildout. Future capex 4-5% for GPU in ForgeAI.

Regionally: Americas $98 million FCF up 50%; EMEA $18 million flat on macro but NRR 115%; APAC $12 million up 80% on Japan.

This yields Rule of 40 at 68, top quartile like Snowflake. We bought back $75 million shares, $450 million authorized remaining. FY2024 FCF guide $550-570 million at 27-28% margin.

Next, our CAC trends, a core efficiency metric. CAC, total sales and marketing expenses divided by new customers, was $428 per new customer in Q3, down 17% year-over-year from $516 and 8% sequentially from Q1. Sixth straight quarter of reduction, payback at 13.2 months from 18, LTV:CAC 4.1x from 3.2x, tied to 118% NRR.

By segment: SMB self-serve $185, down 22% YoY on 28% freemium conversions. Mid-market $620, down 19% with revenue intel tools. Enterprise $2,450, down 12% via ABM.

Regions: NA $390 down 20% on AWS Marketplace; EMEA $510 down 25% on localization; APAC $680 down 10% seq on pilots.

Powered by PLG AI copilot boosting trials 35%, demand gen 2.8x magic number, partners 18% wins. Q4 CAC $410-420 expected.

On the Rule of 40—revenue growth plus non-GAAP EBITDA margin—we scored 48% this quarter, up from 42% prior year, sixth straight above 40. 32% revenue growth to $458 million with ARR at $1.83 billion up 34%, paired with 16% EBITDA margin up 300 bps.

Growth from new logos and 118% NRR, 47 net $1M+ customers including Fortune 100 financials. NA 68% ARR up 35%; EMEA 42%; APAC 28%.

Profitability from opex growth 22% below revenue, sales productivity $1.8M ARR/rep, FCF 14%.

Initiatives like ForgeAI Guardrails cut TCO 40%, boosting upsells. Pillars: AI 30% ARR by FY26, global capex $50M, margin discipline.

Q4 Rule of 40 48-50, FY 46%.

Turning to operating expense breakdown: Total GAAP opex $374 million, up 18% YoY or 82% of revenue vs 88%; non-GAAP $335 million or 73%, down 400 bps.

R&D $142 million up 22% or 31% of revenue, headcount to 850 engineers for ForgeAI Agents v2.0, 60% US, APAC ramp. Down 100 bps on scale.

S&M $189 million up 14% or 33% vs 38%, payback 16 months, PLG shift, ABM ROI 2.5x, events pipeline $20M. Regions US 65%, EMEA 30%, APAC double.

G&A $102 million up 12% or 18% flat %, ERP migration, facilities savings.

Supports 14% EBITDA margin.

Customer mix: Enterprise now 62% ARR up from 52% YoY, boosting NRR 180 bps to 118%; SMB 38%. Added 14 enterprise logos, $450K ACV Fortune 500s for risk analytics.

SMB growth 8% but churn 7%. Americas 68% enterprise, EMEA 28%, APAC 45%.

Enterprise-first: FedRAMP, land-expand 42% ARR from SMBs, PLG freemium. To 65-68% FY25.

Sales efficiency: Average cycle 92 days down 18% YoY. PLG 28 days, sales-led <100K 65 days, enterprise 145 days.

NA 85 days, EMEA 105, APAC 130. Conversions: MQL-close 14.2% up, MQL-SQL 32%, opp-close 42% via intel tools.

Hybrid model, tech stack Clari 95% forecast, magic number 1.4x, payback 14 months. To 85-90 days year-end.

These metrics position us strongly. We're raising full-year guidance: revenue $1.82 billion to $1.88 billion, reflecting H1 strength.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technology update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes across observability and automation. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including zero-trust integrations and 99.99% SLA uptime.

And now Emma Walsh will provide an update on our product roadmap.

Emma Walsh:
Thank you, Lena. We've been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited about our roadmap, which powers our 28% year-over-year ARR growth to $1.83 billion and 118% NRR. As a leader in AI-powered workflow automation and analytics, our roadmap emphasizes AI ubiquity, vertical specialization, and global scale, with PLG at 42% of new ACV.

Recent launches: ForgeAI Insights 2.0 automates 70% routine tasks, adopted by 65% of 12,500 customers like Procter & Gamble, lifting DAUs 22% to 1.2 million, ARPU 15%. Embedded Analytics Marketplace GA with 150+ partners reduced mid-market churn to 4.2%, 18% upsell revenue.

Upcoming: Q4 ForgeAI Agents for multi-step workflows, beta 40% faster cycles, $25-30M ARR FY25. January HyperScale Dashboards 5x faster queries.

Verticals: Forge for Healthcare HITRUST wins, 150% ACV QoQ; Manufacturing IoT for APAC. Regions: NA 72% ARR NRR 132%; EMEA 15% up 32%; APAC 13% 45%.

Composable API-first design, $120M R&D multimodal AI, federated learning. FY25 25-30% ARR growth, 120-125% NRR.

Tyler Brooks:
Thank you, Emma. This quarter our focus was on increasing brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 35% increase in website traffic and a 28% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, particularly ABM and PLG amplification.

Nina Patel:
Thank you, Tyler. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter focused on improving customer support and onboarding. As a result, we saw a 25% increase in customer satisfaction scores, driven by expanded CSMs and proactive telemetry.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star 1 on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative, contributing 25% to Q3 revenue growth through rapid adoption in workflows and analytics. Attach rates are at 45% for eligible accounts, exceeding our 30% initial expectations by wide margin due to proven 3x ROI in pilots. Competitively, we're up against Datadog in observability and ServiceNow in automation, but the landscape favors integrated AI platforms. Our differentiation lies in agentic AI with native multi-cloud support, FedRAMP compliance, and headless APIs for composability—early wins show 2x faster time-to-value than point solutions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Lisa. International is a priority, with APAC targeted for 20% of ARR by FY26. Plans include $50 million investment in edge data centers in Tokyo and Singapore, localized LLMs, and partner ramps with NTT, Alibaba, TCS. Key markets: Japan enterprise, Singapore/HK mid-market, India SMB via marketplaces. Expected ROI 3x over two years on 45% growth trajectory. Challenges: data sovereignty regs, multi-stakeholder cycles—we mitigate with sovereign cloud options and hyperscaler co-sell.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks Raj. Churn is stable at 4.5% annualized, down from 5.5% prior year, through cohort-focused CS and early renewals. NRR trending up to 118% from 115% Q2, driven by expansions. Strategies: CSM density up 15%, Usage Intelligence for proactive upsells, vertical playbooks. Pricing adjustments mid-year were neutral to churn, with 10% uplift on AI tiers offset by volume discounts. Long-term NRR target 120-125% by FY26 as AI attach matures.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Kara Lopez with Barclays.

Kara Lopez:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Kara. As I detailed earlier, blended CAC $428, down 17% YoY, with SMB at $185 payback 8 months, mid-market $620 at 12 months, enterprise $2,450 at 16 months—median 13.2 months overall. Trends improving via PLG 35% trial lift, partners, ABM. LTV:CAC 4.1x supports aggressive scaling.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders through AI innovation and efficient growth. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
